data.title: The Annals of Fulda – the key source on Great Moravia
data.excerpt: The Annals of Fulda (Annales Fuldenses) are the fullest source on the history of Great Moravia in the years 846–902; they were compiled by the monks Einhard, Ruodolf and Meginhard and by anonymous continuators. Because their authors were close to the East Frankish royal court and were guided by its interests, the text has to be read critically, yet it preserves exceptionally valuable information about the first state formation in the territory of present-day Slovakia.

timeline.title: Rastislav becomes ruler of the Moravians
timeline.description: Louis the German installed Rastislav, Mojmír’s nephew, as ruler of the Moravian Slavs.

timeline.title: The siege of Dowina
timeline.description: Louis the German besieged Rastislav in the fortress of Dowina; Rastislav pledged his loyalty by oath, but did not keep it.

timeline.title: The capture of Rastislav
timeline.description: Svatopluk seized Rastislav and handed him over to Carloman; Rastislav was finally blinded.

timeline.title: Slavomír’s revolt and Svatopluk’s return
timeline.description: The Moravians chose the priest Slavomír as their ruler; Svatopluk, released soon afterwards, returned and defeated the Bavarian army at Rastislav’s hillfort.

timeline.title: The death of Svatopluk
timeline.description: Svatopluk, duke of the Moravians, died after exhorting his own people to remain at enmity with their neighbours.

timeline.title: Peace with the Moravians
timeline.description: At the assembly in Regensburg a peace was agreed with the envoys of the Moravians and confirmed by oath; Prince Mojmír II was bound by it as well.

timeline.title: The last recorded battle
timeline.description: The Old Hungarians attacked the territory of the Moravians, but were defeated and put to flight – the last event recorded in the annals.

children.text: The Annals of Fulda (Annales Fuldenses) are the fullest source on the history of Great Moravia in the years 846–902. They were probably compiled by the monks Einhard, Ruodolf and Meginhard (who wrote them down to 882, or 887 respectively) and by anonymous authors, whose work produced the Mainz, Regensburg and Altaich continuations. The contents of the Annals of Fulda have to be approached critically, since the authors were close to the East Frankish royal court and were guided above all by its interests. Even so, the Annals of Fulda contain exceptionally valuable information about the history of the first state formation in the territory of present-day Slovakia – Great Moravia.

blocks.text:
Year 845. Louis received 14 Bohemian dukes who desired the Christian religion, together with their retinues, and ordered them to be baptised in the week after the Epiphany (after 6 January). In the autumn he summoned a general assembly at Paderborn in Saxony, where he received, heard and dismissed the embassies of his brothers and further those of the Northmen, the Slavs and the Bulgars.
Year 846.
Year 855
Year 857. Bishop Otakar, the count palatine Hruodolt and Ernest, the son of Duke Ernest, were sent with their armies into Bohemia, and they succeeded in taking the fortress of Duke Vistrach, which had held out for many years, and drove from it his son Slavitéch, who at that time ruled there without restraint. After his flight he took refuge with Rastislav. Thereupon his brother, whom Slavitéch had earlier driven out and who had been living with Čestibor of the Sorbs, came submissively to the king, and the king appointed him the new duke.
Year 858.
In July, when the assembled and marshalled armies had already set out, great cares suddenly fell upon the king in the middle of the day. For messengers came from the west, the abbot Adalhart and Count Oto, and asked him to come in person to the aid of a people that had fallen into danger and distress.
Year 861. Carloman, the eldest of the king’s sons, also strove for a coup. He drove out the dukes entrusted with the defence of the Pannonian and Carantanian frontier and divided the march among his own adherents. And this stirred the mind of the king, who suspected his son of rebellion.
Year 862. Carloman, having received guarantees of peace and of his own safety, came to Regensburg. There he rendered account, convicted his opponents and was reconciled with his father. He confirmed by oath that in future he would devise nothing treacherous against his father’s lawful authority. Carloman then returned peacefully to his own domain, and the king set out for Mainz, where he received his nephew Lothar, who had come to negotiate with him. 
Year 863
Year 864. In August King Louis set out with a great army across the Danube and besieged Rastislav in a certain fortress which in the language of that people is called Dowina (that is, Maiden). Rastislav, however, did not dare to fight the royal armies, and when he was convinced that he had nowhere to escape, he was compelled by circumstances to hand over as many hostages, and such as, the king desired. Moreover, together with all his magnates he pledged by oath that he would always keep faith with the king, which, however, he did not keep at all.
Year 865. One of the Frankish magnates, Count Verinhar, was accused before King Louis of having allegedly incited Rastislav against the king. He was therefore deprived of his public offices.
Year 866. Louis, the younger son of Louis, took it ill that the king had taken certain estates from him and given them to his elder brother Carloman. He therefore began to work harm to his father. He sent his messengers throughout Thuringia and Saxony, sought to win everyone to his side and incited them to rebel against the king. For his purposes he also won over the counts Verinhar, Uto and Berengar, whom the king had earlier deposed, and promised to restore to them their former dignities. In addition he sent Henry, the commander of his military retinue, to Rastislav with an urgent request that he should not refuse his support for this conspiracy. When the king learned of it, he left Carloman to protect Bavaria and quickly went to Francia. The king’s adherents, gathered from all sides at Frankfurt, received him with honour, and Louis easily suppressed the conspiracy that had been devised.
Year 869
In August King Louis assembled an army and divided it into three corps. He entrusted the suppression of Sorbian insolence to his namesake and placed the Thuringians and the Saxons at his disposal. 
Year 870.
And then, at the beginning of November, King Louis advanced into Bavaria, and there, after taking counsel with his men, he gave orders that before him 
Year 871. Svatopluk, Rastislav’s nephew, was accused of disloyalty before Carloman and imprisoned. The Moravian Slavs, believing that their duke had perished, set over themselves as ruler a certain priest Slavomír, who was a kinsman of the imprisoned duke, and threatened him with death if he refused to rule over them. He therefore agreed under compulsion, began to fight against Carloman’s commanders Engilschalk and Wilhelm and tried to drive them from the places they had occupied. They, however, fought the rebels with great effort, and when they had killed some of them, they forced Slavomír to withdraw.
Meanwhile Carloman released Svatopluk, because no one could prove against him the crimes of which he had been accused. Honoured with royal gifts, he returned to his kingdom at the head of Carloman’s army, as if he meant to fight Slavomír. For so he had cunningly promised Carloman, if he would allow him to return to his homeland. Yet men who are incautious and too sure of themselves are often overtaken by disgrace, and this happened to this army too. While the others were building a camp, Svatopluk entered Rastislav’s old hillfort and at once broke faith and forgot his oath, which is, after all, a Slavic custom. He spent his strength and his abilities not on defeating Slavomír, but on avenging the injury that Carloman had done him. With a great army he fell upon the unsuspecting and little watchful Bavarians in their camp and took many of them alive. Almost all the rest he killed, except those who had prudently withdrawn from the camp beforehand. And so all the joy of the Noricans at their many earlier victories was turned into mourning and lamentation. When Carloman heard of it, he was greatly dismayed at the destruction of his army. Compelled by circumstances, he ordered all the hostages who were in his kingdom to be gathered and returned them to Svatopluk. He himself, however, received only a single man, Ratbod, and he half dead.
In October the king held counsel with his men at Frankfurt. From there he went to Bavaria, and against the Bohemians, who were attempting an invasion of his empire, he sent the protectors of those lands, Bishop Arno and Count Rudolf, and others with them. The enemy, however, had fortified a certain place with a mighty rampart, leaving only a narrow path at the very entrance as a snare against those who guarded the frontiers. If any of them chanced to enter there, he would be killed, for from the narrow path there was no escape anywhere. At that 
Year 872
Year 873. To the assembly near Worms there also came a certain Alemann, Berechtram, whom the Moravian Slavs had captured in the previous year. Duke Svatopluk had released him with a commission to deliver his message to the king. He also had to pledge by oath that he would carry it out.
Year 874. King Louis, on his return (from Verona), met his sons Carloman and Louis for talks at Forchheim, and there he also received Svatopluk’s envoys, who asked for peace and promised loyalty. The envoys were led by the priest John of Venice, who declared and confirmed by oath (so that the king might believe him without any doubt) that Svatopluk would remain loyal to the king to the end of his days and would pay yearly the tribute fixed by the king. In return, however, he asked to be allowed to rule in quiet and to live in peace. The king also heard the embassy of the Bohemians and dismissed them. Then he departed for Bavaria.
Year 884. The emperor (Charles III the Fat) held talks with Svatopluk on the frontier of the Noricans and the Slavs.

blocks.text:
Year 882. The king (Charles III the Fat) stayed in Germania and before Christmas summoned an assembly at Worms. When he had received there various embassies of the Moravians and of other peoples, heard them and set public affairs in order, he returned to Alemannia.
Year 884. When the king returned to Alemannia, a general assembly was held at Colmar. There the Bavarians were ordered to organise an armed expedition into Italy against Vito.
A great disaster then befell Pannonia
“Every kingdom – says Jesus – that is divided against itself 
becomes unsteady, nor does anything discordant endure. 
Therefore, most beautiful land, treachery and affliction pursue you, 
therefore, Pannonia, once happy, does suffering pursue you.”
And so 
These shameful deeds, brought about by the rash conduct of young men 
Shortly afterwards the duke gathered very numerous military detachments from all the Slavic lands and invaded Pannonia with them. He slaughtered furiously and bloodily like a wolf and laid waste the greater part of it with fire and sword. He overthrew and destroyed everything, and so this disaster may with full right be described in verse:
“This is the lament of the fatherland and at the same time its mournful burial.”
When the suffering caused by the aforesaid youthful rashness had ended, after the passing of one year the duke returned home with his army without losses.
But in the following year, in which we are writing down these events, the duke again gathered a multitude of troops and invaded Pannonia as an enemy, in order now to devour with his jaws, like a wolf, everything that had still remained untouched there.
The emperor (Charles III the Fat) advanced eastwards through Bavaria and near the river Tulln held a meeting on the hill called Komianus. 
Year 885.
Year 888. In the city of Regensburg King Arnulf received the magnates of the Bavarians, the East Franks, the Saxons, the Thuringians, the Alemanni and a great part of the Slavs, and there he worthily celebrated both Christmas and Easter.
Year 890
Year 891
Year 892
From there, in September, he also sent his envoys with gifts to the Bulgars and to their king Vladimir, to renew the earlier peace. He also asked that the Moravians should not be allowed to buy salt from them. Because of the snares of Duke Svatopluk, however, the envoys could not set out overland, but sailed by ship from Braslav’s domain along the river Odra as far as the Kulpa and then down the Sava into Bulgaria. There the king received them with honour, and in May they returned by the same road by which they had come.
Year 893. Before the forty-day fast the king (Arnulf) visited monasteries and bishoprics throughout the territory of the West Franks in order to pray there. Engilschalk, a man of youthful daring, who after abducting the daughter of the king’s concubine had for a time fled as an exile to the Moravians, shortly afterwards obtained pardon and became margrave of the Eastern March. There he acted harshly against the Bavarian magnates in the matters entrusted to him. By the decision of these magnates, when he entered the royal palace at Regensburg suspecting nothing, he was blinded without having been brought before the king. Wilhelm too, the son of his uncle, was accused of high treason and beheaded, because he had sent his messengers to Duke Svatopluk. And his brother, who was hiding among the Moravians as an exile, fell together with many others a victim to the treacherous cunning of the said duke.
The king therefore set out on the march and again invaded the kingdom of Duke Svatopluk at the head of his army. When he had plundered the greater part of his territory, he returned with great difficulty to Bavaria because of the snares that (the Moravians) had prepared for him

Year 897. 
Year 898
Year 899
Shortly afterwards 
Meanwhile, however, Isanrik was ever more boldly strengthening his power against the king’s interests. The king bore this with displeasure and, because he was already sick and weak, ordered the town of Mautern, in which Isanrik was staying, to be attacked by a fleet, and so it was done. At first he did indeed offer resistance, but when he saw the bravery and the superior numbers of the royal army, which had besieged and assaulted him, he had to surrender, together with his wife and his retinue, to the emperor (and king).
The king then entrusted him to guards, that they might watch over him on the road to Regensburg. He, however, feared punishment, took to flight and took refuge as far away as among the Moravians. As before, so now too, with their support and help he seized part of the kingdom into his own power.
When Engilmar, bishop of Passau, died, his see was taken, with royal consent and against the ordinances of the fathers of the bishops, by a certain Alemann, Wiching, whom the pope had earlier appointed bishop of Moravia. Shortly afterwards, however, against the king’s will, he was deposed from the episcopal see by the canonical judgment of Archbishop Theotmar and of the other bishops subject to him. In his place Richar was at the same time appointed bishop.
Year 900. The Bavarians invaded the kingdom of the Moravians through Bohemia, whose people they had taken as allies, and for three weeks they ravaged the land there with fire. In the end they returned home without any harm.
Meanwhile, however, the Avars, who are called Hungarians, laid waste Italy and killed several bishops in the process. In a single one-day battle they killed 20,000 Italians who had offered them resistance. They themselves then returned by the same road by which they had come, laying waste in addition the greater part of Pannonia.
Then, cunningly asking for peace, they sent their envoys to the Bavarians in order to reconnoitre that country. This brought, alas, the first evil and disaster such as had never before been experienced in Bavaria. For unexpectedly 
Meanwhile, however, 
Year 901.
Meanwhile, however, the Hungarians invaded the southern part of their kingdom and plundered Carinthia.
The Hungarians invaded Carinthia and were defeated in a battle that took place on a Saturday.
In the same year.
Year 902. The Hungarians attacked the territory of the Moravians. In the fighting, however, they were defeated and took to flight.
